needs_user.question: Existing Cursor users still have Silver Bullet hook entries in ~/.cursor/hooks.json and plugin caches. I deleted the whole uninstall path (post-release-uninstall.sh cursor branch, strip-cursor-sb-hooks.py) so no code writes into ~/.cursor. Keep a minimal one-time cleanup?
needs_user.recommendation: Yes: ship a documented manual-cleanup note (CHANGELOG/docs) now; if you want automation, add a tiny strip-only script (removes entries whose command points at a Silver Bullet hooks dir, atomic write, backup, never adds anything) invoked only by an explicit command, not by install/doctor.

needs_user.question: silver-multi-ai-task (and silver-deep-research-multi-ai live dispatch) declare Cursor as the only v1 execution host and the default backend (cursor_default_pool, cursor_host_adapter.py, provision-cursor-agents.sh, live_dispatch.py run_cursor_worker, host-matrix-v1.json). Removing Cursor leaves OCG-only dispatch and no supported host. Remove the skills, or port to an OCG-only/claude/codex host?
needs_user.recommendation: Retire the cursor backend and make OCG the sole backend with host claude/codex, as a dedicated package with its own 100% coverage tests; I left this subsystem untouched (files restored) rather than half-edit it.

needs_user.question: The review-fix-ladder is built around Cursor custom subagents (sb-* names), a Cursor ladder resolver (resolve_cursor_ladder, cursor_sb_agents config), the subscription-first / cursor_task / cursor_fallback decision logic, hook state (subscription_quota_fallback) and rfl_launcher_policy's Cursor/Grok/Composer rungs. Remove the Cursor ladder and subscription-first mechanism entirely (redesign for claude/codex spawns)?
needs_user.recommendation: Yes, in a dedicated RFL package; it needs a ladder redesign (default host, rung naming, guard enforcement), not a mechanical delete. Left untouched here; scripts/lib/cursor-sb-agents and install-cursor-sb-agents.sh are gone so the resolver now falls back to its file checks.

needs_user.question: Matchers 'CallMcpTool|MCP' in hooks.json (and CallMcpTool handling in hooks) are Cursor's MCP tool name. Kept because Claude/Codex MCP naming is not covered by 'MCP' alone. Drop 'CallMcpTool'?
needs_user.recommendation: Verify Claude (mcp__*) and Codex MCP tool names against hook payloads first; then drop CallMcpTool and widen the matcher to the real names.
